Oracle Database 19c에서 UPDATE가 행 잠금(TX)과: A 10-step animated lesson that follows how, in Oracle Database 19c, an UPDATE takes a row lock (TX) and a table lock (TM), and how sessions that want the same row queue up on enq: TX - row lock contention. It also covers why reads are never blocked, how to find and clear the blocking session with V$SESSION, and deadlocks (ORA-00060).

12시 10분, 주문 저장 버튼이 돌기만 한다: 12:10 p.m.: the order save button just spins
점심시간 주문이 몰리는 12시 10분, 앱 담당자의 전화가 옵니다. \": At 12:10, in the lunchtime order rush, the app owner calls: "When I press Save, the screen freezes." The server CPU is idle and the disks are quiet. The database does not look slow, yet orders are not being saved.
이럴 때 세션은 일을 하고 있는 것이 아니라 <span class=\"t: In a case like this the sessions are not working, they are waiting, and Oracle records exactly what they wait for. This lesson follows what is behind that wait: locks.
CPU가 놀고 있는데 응답이 없다면 \"느림\"이 아니라 \"대기\"를: If the CPU is idle but nothing responds, suspect waiting before slowness. Waits often trace back to a single cause, so once found they clear quickly.
UPDATE는 고친 행마다 잠금(TX)을 건다: An UPDATE locks every row it changes (TX)
20분 전, 배치 담당자가 세션 142에서 주문 상태를 고치는 UPDAT: Twenty minutes ago, the batch owner ran an UPDATE that changes order status in session 142. According to Concepts, a transaction acquires a row lock (TX) for each row modified by INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE or SELECT … FOR UPDATE.
이 잠금은 문장이 끝나도 풀리지 않습니다. 문서대로 행 잠금은 트랜잭션이: The lock is not released when the statement ends. As the documentation says, a row lock exists until the transaction issues COMMIT or ROLLBACK. The batch owner ran the UPDATE, did not commit, and went to lunch.
SQL*Plus나 SQL Developer에서 DML을 손으로 돌리면 커: When you run DML by hand in SQL*Plus or SQL Developer, someone has to commit. "1 row updated." does not mean the change is saved; it means you now hold the lock.
잠금은 메모리의 목록이 아니라 블록 안에 적힌다: Locks are written in the block, not in a list in memory
행 잠금은 어디에 있을까요? Concepts에 따르면 모든 세그먼트 블록: Where does a row lock live? According to Concepts, the header of every segment block holds an ITL (interested transaction list), and its entries describe which transactions have rows locked. The lock information is stored in the data block that contains the locked row.
그래서 오라클은 잠긴 행이 아무리 많아도 메모리에 행 잠금 목록을 따로: So no matter how many rows are locked, Oracle keeps no separate list of row locks in memory and never escalates row locks into a table lock. Change a million rows and only those million rows are locked.
다른 DB를 써 본 분은 \"잠금이 많아지면 테이블 전체가 잠긴다\"고: If you have used other databases you may have learned that "many locks turn into a table lock". Oracle does not do that, according to the documentation. The ITL details in this lesson come from a summary of the Concepts chapter.
~ 잠금 목록을 메모리에 두지 않음: ~ no lock list kept in memory
조회 세션은 막히지 않는다: Undo로 커밋된 값을 본다: The query session is not blocked: it sees committed values through undo
그사이 세션 305가 같은 주문 1001을 조회합니다. 문서는 데이터를: Meanwhile session 305 queries the same order 1001. The documentation says readers and writers of data do not block one another. Session 305 does not wait at the locked row; it gets its result right away.
다만 세션 305가 보는 값은 142가 고친 <code>PAID</cod: But what session 305 sees is not PAID from session 142; it is the old committed value NEW. Oracle keeps the value from before the change in undo and uses it to rebuild the block as of the query's start. The lesson "Undo and read consistency" looks at this in detail.
그래서 \"조회는 되는데 저장만 안 된다\"는 신고는 행 잠금의 전형적인: That is why "queries work, only saving hangs" is the classic picture of a row lock. A working query screen does not mean the database is fine.
~ Undo로 커밋된 값(NEW)을 봄: ~ sees the committed value (NEW) through undo
같은 행을 고치려는 세션은 줄을 선다: A session that wants to change the same row waits in line
이제 주문 화면의 세션 201이 같은 주문 1001을 고치려 합니다. 문: Now session 201 from the order screen tries to change the same order 1001. As the documentation says, a writer of a row blocks a concurrent writer of the same row. Session 201 sees in the ITL that transaction 142 holds the row and waits for that transaction to end.
이때 기록되는 대기 이벤트가 <code>enq: TX - row lock: The wait event recorded here is enq: TX - row lock contention. The Database Reference says it occurs when a session tries to update or delete a row another session is modifying, and is released when the holder commits or rolls back. It also occurs when inserting a duplicate key into a unique index.
기다리는 세션은 기본으로 시간 제한 없이 기다립니다. 앱의 연결 풀이 이: By default the waiting session waits with no time limit. If the app's connection pool fills up with such sessions, even orders unrelated to the locked rows cannot be saved. That is how a lunchtime incident grows.
× enq: TX - row lock contention 대기: × waits on enq: TX - row lock contention
DML은 테이블에도 잠금(TM)을 하나 건다: DML also puts one lock (TM) on the table
세션 142는 행 잠금 말고도 ORDERS 테이블에 <span class: Besides its row locks, session 142 holds one table lock (TM) on the ORDERS table. In the Database Reference list of enqueue names, TM is the DML enqueue and TX the transaction enqueue. The TM taken by DML is in the Row Exclusive (RX) mode described in Concepts, which still allows other sessions' DML.
이 잠금이 막는 것은 테이블 구조를 바꾸는 DDL입니다. 문서는 테이블: What this lock blocks is DDL that changes the table's structure. The documentation says table locks prevent DDL operations that would conflict with the transaction. If someone tried to add a column or rebuild an index on this table at lunchtime, that work would also run into this transaction.
그래서 운영 중인 테이블의 DDL은 이 테이블에 오래 열린 트랜잭션이 없: So before DDL on a live table, first check that no long-open transaction is on it. The V$SESSION query used in stage 3 lesson 27 is that check.
~ DML끼리는 통과, 충돌하는 DDL은 막힘: ~ other DML passes; conflicting DDL is blocked

사례: V$SESSION으로 막는 세션을 찾는다: Case: find the blocking session with V$SESSION
DBA는 먼저 무엇을 기다리는지 봅니다. Performance Tunin: The DBA first looks at what is being waited for. According to the Performance Tuning Guide, V$SESSION holds each session's wait information together with the blocking session responsible for the current wait (its ID and status). Selecting only sessions whose BLOCKING_SESSION is not empty shows the whole queue at a glance.
기다리는 세션 셋이 모두 142를 가리킵니다. 이어서 142가 누구인지(: All three waiting sessions point to 142. Next, look at who 142 is (account, program, logon time, seconds since the last call). It is the batch account, INACTIVE for 20 minutes: holding locks while doing no work.
STATUS가 INACTIVE라고 무해한 것은 아닙니다. 커밋하지 않은: INACTIVE does not mean harmless. An uncommitted transaction keeps its locks while the session sits idle. You run exactly this query in DBA labs stage 3, lesson 27.
사례: 확인받고 정리하면 줄이 한 번에 풀린다: Case: clear it after confirming, and the queue drains at once
가장 좋은 해결은 배치 담당자가 돌아와 COMMIT이나 ROLLBACK을: The best fix is for the batch owner to come back and COMMIT or ROLL BACK. If they cannot be reached and business is stopped, the DBA gets confirmation from the owner or team lead and ends the session with ALTER SYSTEM KILL SESSION '142,31175'. Giving both SID and SERIAL# makes sure the right session is ended.
끊긴 세션의 커밋하지 않은 변경은 롤백되고, 롤백이 끝나면 잠금이 풀립니: The ended session's uncommitted changes are rolled back, and when the rollback finishes the locks are released. At that moment session 201, first in line, gets the row and finishes its UPDATE. The other sessions follow, and the order screen comes back.
KILL은 그 사람이 하던 작업을 버리는 일입니다. 반드시 확인을 받고,: KILL throws away that person's work. Always get confirmation, and afterwards tell the owner what was rolled back so it can be rerun. The DBA labs stage 7 graduation mission is this scene.
사례: 서로를 기다리면 오라클이 한쪽을 깨운다: Case: when two sessions wait for each other, Oracle wakes one
다른 날, 세션 142가 주문 1001을, 세션 201이 주문 1002를: Another day, session 142 changes order 1001 first and session 201 changes order 1002. Then 142 tries to change 1002 and 201 tries 1001. Each waits for the row the other holds, so neither can finish. This is a deadlock.
Concepts에 따르면 오라클은 교착 상태를 자동으로 찾아 풀고, 한: According to Concepts, Oracle detects deadlocks automatically, resolves them, and returns ORA-00060: deadlock detected to one session. In the documentation's example, what is rolled back is one statement, not that session's whole transaction. The session that got the error still holds its other locks, so the app must COMMIT or ROLL BACK before the other side is released.
교착 상태는 DBA가 KILL할 일이 아니라 앱이 고칠 일인 경우가 많습: A deadlock is usually for the app to fix, not for the DBA to KILL. If every program changes multiple rows in the same order (for example, ascending order number), it does not happen.
× ORA-00060 (한 세션, 문장 하나 롤백): × ORA-00060 (one session, one statement rolled back)
정리: 쓰기는 행마다 잠그고, 기다림은 기록된다: Recap: writes lock row by row, and every wait is recorded
DML은 고친 행마다 TX 잠금을, 테이블에는 TM 잠금을 겁니다. 잠금: DML takes a TX lock for each changed row and a TM lock on the table. Lock information is written in the block's ITL and released when the transaction commits or rolls back. Readers see committed values through undo and are never blocked; only writers of the same row queue up.
줄을 서는 동안 오라클은 무엇을 누구 때문에 기다리는지(<code>EVE: While sessions wait, Oracle records what they wait for and because of whom (EVENT, BLOCKING_SESSION) in V$SESSION. The DBA's job is to read that record, find the cause, and clear it after confirmation.
\"COMMIT의 여정\"이 커밋이 무엇을 쓰는지 보여 줬다면, 이 레슨: "The journey of a COMMIT" showed what a commit writes; this lesson shows what stays behind when you do not commit. A commit saves your work and also gives your locks back.
~ TX: 행마다 · TM: 테이블마다: ~ TX: per row · TM: per table
